subject.title: [Feature]: Support to edit system prompt template

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class user-editable override contract for OpenClaw-owned system prompt sections such as Safety, Tool Call Style, OpenClaw Control, and Self-Update?
rationale: The request changes model-facing safety guidance and prompt precedence, while current code intentionally exposes narrower provider, hook, channel, bootstrap, and SDK prompt surfaces, so automation cannot choose the permanent product and security boundary.

options.title: Approve scoped section overrides
options.body: Add a narrow named-section text override model with explicit edit authority, precedence, security docs, prompt-cache behavior, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep core sections fixed
options.body: Reject user-editable core sections and document provider overlays, channel prompts, plugin hooks, and bootstrap files as the supported customization paths.

options.title: Defer to narrower prompt work
options.body: Let identity-line, config-rules, include, and hook-replacement work proceed independently while leaving broad Safety/template editing unresolved.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped section overrides
recommendation.body: Add a narrow named-section text override model with explicit edit authority, precedence, security docs, prompt-cache behavior, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent history on provider-owned prompt contributions and the OpenClaw-owned prompt boundary this decision would change.
